# Ghana

> [!summary] Data available
> Medium dish coverage: [[World Wide Dishes]] 23 dishes (19 Ghana-only) in Twi, Hausa and Akan, [[WorldCuisines]] 13 and [[FmLAMA]] 5. Ethnobotany is relatively strong ([[Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases|Duke]] 583 records, mostly Ayensu); no FCT in the vault, but the West African FCT sits inside the FAO/INFOODS candidate.

## Foods & dishes
- [[World Wide Dishes]]: **23 dishes (19 Ghana-only)**; free-text ingredients, no amounts or method, plus eating context (time of day, occasion, utensils, local-language name). Languages Hausa 6, Twi 4, Akan 3; Southern Ghana and Volta Region. Examples: kontomire stew, banku with okro soup, wasawasa, yoroyoro, rice balls.
- [[WorldCuisines]]: 13 dishes (5 Ghana-only: waakye, fufu, kokonte, kenkey, kelewele); Wikipedia-style descriptions naming ingredients, no amounts.
- [[FmLAMA]]: 5 dishes (61 rows), e.g. tuo zaafi, fufu, kelewele, peanut soup; Wikidata ingredient lists, no amounts.

## Ingredients & food composition
- No national FCT is in the vault. The [[FAO INFOODS global databases]] candidate (priority 2, directory of 308 tables) includes the FAO/INFOODS **West African Food Composition Table (WAFCT)**, a regional table for the ECOWAS countries including Ghana; processing it is the most direct way to get local foods (fonio, cowpea, shea, baobab, leafy sauces). Until then, use [[USDA FoodData Central]] by name matching.
- Plant occurrence: [[CMAUP]] 134 plants.

## Compounds & traditional medicine
- [[Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases|Duke]]: **583 ethnobotany records (168 taxa)**, the second-most in Sub-Saharan Africa, mostly from Ayensu (fever, dysentery, laxative, dentifrice).
- [[KNApSAcK Family]] lists Ghana on its World map, but African flag pages were not scraped (counts unknown). [[NPASS]] has 1 pair.
- Compound → effect chains come from the global backbone via [[Global]] ([[FooDB]], [[CTD]], [[Phenol-Explorer]], [[SpiceRx]], [[DDID]] for food–drug interactions).

## Gaps
- WAFCT not yet processed; no recipes with amounts.
- Northern Ghana food is thin; no Ghanaian herbal-medicine database beyond Duke.
